class.name: ScriptTestExecution
class.brief_description: Guards a single FoundryScript callable with timeout, abort, and structured completion semantics.
class.description: [ScriptTestExecution] is a low-level primitive for project test runners. It runs one method call under an execution guard that can time out tight script loops, abort cooperatively, and return a structured [ScriptTestExecutionResult] instead of hanging the process. When the guarded call suspends on [code]await[/code], [method callv] returns a pending [ScriptFunctionState] handle whose [signal ScriptFunctionState.completed] emits the final result. Each [ScriptTestExecution] instance is single-use per guarded call: calling [method callv] again while a previous call is still pending returns [constant ScriptTestExecutionResult.STATUS_RUNTIME_ERROR]. Nested guards are supported. [method ScriptTestAbort.abort_current] and checkpoint enforcement always target the innermost active guard on the calling thread. [b]Cleanup guarantees[/b] After a timeout or abort the engine unwinds the guarded script stack, releases parked coroutine handles, clears their signal connections, and restores the thread-local guard state so the runner can continue with [code]after_each[/code] and the rest of the suite. The engine does [i]not[/i] undo test side effects such as spawned nodes, files, singletons, or global environment changes. [b]Known limitations[/b] A single blocking native call cannot be interrupted; enforcement happens at script line checkpoints and [code]await[/code] boundaries only. Release-profile compiled-bytecode exports strip line checkpoints, so CPU-loop timeouts fall back to await-boundary enforcement there. Editor and headless project test runs retain line checkpoints.

method.name: callv
method.description: Runs [param method] on [param object] with [param args] under this guard. Returns a [ScriptTestExecutionResult] immediately when the call completes synchronously, or a pending [ScriptFunctionState] handle when the call suspends.

members.member: When [code]true[/code], error-severity diagnostics reported on the guarded thread flag an abort at the next checkpoint. Defaults to [code]false[/code]; the engine never decides by itself that a diagnostic fails a test.
Maximum wall time for the guarded call. [code]0.0[/code] disables timeout enforcement.
